header.name: Trent Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Trent (NSE: TRENT), part of the Tata Group, operates a retail business; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹20,074 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹5,873 crore, 21.9% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 11.2% against 10.2%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹464 crore, 23.1% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 30 Oct 2026, the first session after the result, TRENT shares rose 5.44% while the NIFTY 50 rose 0.51% and the NIFTY INDIA CONSUMPTION index rose 0.29%; allowing for the market's move, TRENT's own move was +4.71%, about 2.44 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the consumption (thematic) sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹3,204 (NSE close, 16 Nov 2026), the reinvestment-phase discounted cash flow model (Template B, since TRENT's median return on invested capital of 29.6% is above its 14.00% cost of capital) does not reach the price at any revenue growth up to 60% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 11.5%; with revenue growing at its FY23–FY26 rate of 34.5%, it does at an operating margin of 28.0%.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the operating margin (two percentage points either way: a model value of ₹749 to ₹1,281 a share) and to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹854 to ₹1,222 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹1 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹2k crore of cash and treasury.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY23–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY23 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of TRENT's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.name: Bear

scenarios.name: Base

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.what: Revenue grows 2 points a year faster than its FY23-FY26 rate for five years and the margin rises 1 point.

valuation.rule_note: The cost of debt and long-run growth are set by fixed rules and not reviewed by a person.

template_b.name: Template B · reinvestment phase
template_b.why: Template A needs free cash flow to the firm to be positive in at least three of the last four years, and here it was ₹2,731 crore in FY24, −₹470 crore in FY25 and −₹222 crore in FY26.
template_b.test: Template B runs the same model but asks a different question of the past: does the capital being reinvested earn more than it costs? The median return on invested capital over FY24–FY26 was 29.6%, against a cost of capital of 14.00%. Its bear and bull cases are set around the history growth rate, because the latest years are the reinvestment itself.
tiles: economic profit after year 10, today's value
template_b.first_positive: In the base case, free cash flow turns positive in FY32: until then the growth is paid for by reinvestment, while economic profit is already positive.

flags.title: The price is beyond what the model can reach
flags.text: The model cannot reach the price at any revenue growth up to 60% a year, so the page says 'more than 60%' instead of forcing a number. This is a statement about the model's range and assumptions, not a forecast and not a view on the shares.

flags.title: One year of free cash flow comes from shrinking capital
flags.text: FY24's positive free cash flow comes mostly from a fall in invested capital, as lease liabilities and right-of-use assets fell sharply that year; the filings read here do not say why.

flags.title: The reinvestment version of the model is used
flags.text: Template A did not apply (free cash flow not positive in at least 3 of the last 4 years), so this page uses Template B, which is judged on return on capital and assumes today's return on capital lasts.

flags.title: The exchange's files contain errors
flags.text: 6 reconciliation checks fail on the exchange's own files, each with a recorded reason. They are marked as explained, not passed, and the figure as filed is used, never a corrected one.

flags.title: FY22 is left out
flags.text: Trent's FY22 exchange file reports every amount 100 times too small (a units error in the filing) and no later filing repeats FY22, so the history starts in FY23 and the free-cash-flow test covers three years.

flags.title: Prices are adjusted for a bonus issue
flags.text: Prices before the 1:2 bonus issue are divided by 1.5 and the share count is multiplied by 1.5, so returns, the chart and market value compare like with like. NSE's own files are not adjusted.

limitations: Template B (reinvestment phase): the same single-stage fade model, judged on return on capital rather than past free cash flow. The base case assumes today's return on capital lasts; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.

FY22 is left out: Trent's FY22 exchange XBRL filing reports every amount 100 times too small (a units error in the filing), and no later filing repeats FY22. The history starts in FY23, so the free-cash-flow test covers three years, not four.

Prices before Trent's 1:2 bonus issue (ex 4 June 2026) are divided by 1.5, and the share count dated 31 March 2026 is multiplied by 1.5, so returns, the chart, the 52-week range and market value compare like with like. NSE's own files are not adjusted.
FY24's positive free cash flow comes mostly from a fall in invested capital, as lease liabilities and right-of-use assets fell sharply that year; the filings read here do not say why.

From FY23 the figures come from the exchange XBRL filings; the lease lines for FY23–FY25 come from the results PDFs (text layer, checked against the printed subtotals and, for FY26, against the XBRL).
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
